messages:
maya: Heads-up — since 09:15 we've seen a small spike of svc-a -> svc-b failures in eu-west. Proxy logs show TLS fallbacks and ALPN negotiation oddities. Not a full outage but degraded p99 latency and a few 502s.

samir: I saw that too. Correlating with an RBAC tweak yesterday evening (scoped KMS permissions). Could be the proxy failing to unwrap ephemeral keys, falling back to older TLS profile. cc @jules @ashley

maya: sample proxy snippet from 09:16:02: 
```
ALPN: requested="h2" negotiated=""
handshake_error: ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
peer_cert: CN=svc-b-eu.internal tls_version=TLSv1.3 cipher=TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
key_unwrap: ERROR KMS AccessDenied principal=arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/svc-proxy action=kms:Decrypt
```

jules: If KMS unwrap fails the proxy should reject, not downgrade. Weird that there was a downgrade. Could be an intermediate proxy in front of svc-b that has fallback policy. Do we have the ingress proxy logs?

ashley: grabbing ingress logs now. Also checking audit logs for KMS denies and the actor that triggered the RBAC change.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Deployment "rbac/svc-proxy-kms-scope" merged by samir at 2026-03-22T18:04:12Z.

samir: That was me — I scoped the svc-proxy role to remove kms:Decrypt for the old service-account name (we were trying to prevent cross-tenant unwrap). I thought svc-proxy used a different role binding. Didn't expect it to hit live.

maya: Okay — plausible chain: KMS deny -> proxy can't unwrap ephemeral key -> some proxy stack (maybe an older ALB/NLB path) falls back to a different TLS profile that accepts client certs differently, leading to handshake ALPN mismatch. Need to confirm.

ashley: Audit logs show repeated KMS:Decrypt Deny from principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/svc-proxy at 09:15:58-09:17:10. Actor for RBAC change: samir (deploy-bot applied PR #4821).

jules: Notes for triage: 1) Repro locally by forcing KMS denies on a canary proxy. 2) Check proxy config: ensure it treats KMS unwrap failure as fatal and does not fallback to legacy listener. 3) Add telemetry to tag fallback decisions in traces.

maya: Quick runbook proposal: 
- Immediate: rollback RBAC change for svc-proxy (re-add kms:Decrypt) to restore unwrap.
- Short term: patch proxy to explicitly abort on unwrap failure (no fallback path).
- Follow-up: audit log retention check and add alert when KMS unwrap denies spike > 1/min.

samir: I'm prepared to rollback now (PR #4829). Deploy will take ~5m. Any objections?

ashley: Go ahead. While rolling back I'll open an audit ticket to map all principals that need unwrap rights. Also increasing audit retention for KMS logs in eu-west to 90d for now.

sec-bot: Alert created: SECURITY-2026-042 — KMS unwrap deny spike in eu-west. Links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/SEC-2026-042

jules: After rollback we should run a canary traffic run from svc-a to svc-b and watch for: handshake success, ALPN negotiated to h2, no decrypt denies, and no listener fallback. Also run TLS config scanner across proxies to ensure no listeners have permissive fallback policy.

maya: Ashley, can you paste the IAM policy diff you reverted? Want to capture the exact principal path so we can update docs.

ashley: policy diff (simplified): 
```
- Resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/ephemeral-key
  Action: kms:Decrypt
  Principal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/old-svc-account
+ Resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/ephemeral-key
  Action: kms:Decrypt
  Principal: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/svc-proxy
```
I removed svc-proxy entry during a cleanup; rollback re-adds it.

maya: Good — we need a postmortem action: an RBAC policy checklist for KMS-scoped resources that lists all service principals that must keep unwrap. Add a rule to require a canary test before merge for RBAC changes that touch KMS.

samir: Rollback complete. Monitoring shows KMS denies dropped to 0 within 2m and p99 latency starting to normalize.

opsbot: deploy-bot: Rollback "rbac/svc-proxy-kms-scope" applied by samir at 2026-03-23T09:23:44Z.

jules: Nice. Next steps assigned: maya (postmortem + runbook update), ashley (audit retention + mapping), samir (PR for safer RBAC gating), and me (proxy patch to abort on unwrap fail).

maya: I'll draft a short incident write-up and assign the follow-ups to the incident board. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
